αἰθομένας: αἴθω/αἴθομαι — burn, blaze; pres. part. mid. fem. acc. pl. (agreeing with δαΐδας): ’burning’
αἱ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. pl. ’they’, referring to the ships (αἱ δ’ ... ἔπλεον) · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of women (αἱ δ’ ὅτε ... ἵκοντο ’and when they came’) · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of the mules (αἱ δ’ ὦκα λίπον ’and they quickly left’)
αὐτοῦ: αὐτός — self; masc. gen. sg., intensive with a possessive (ἑὸν αὐτοῦ ’his own very own’): ’of himself’ · also the fixed adv. αὐτοῦ, ’there, on the spot, right here’ · also plain gen. sg. pronoun, unemphatic ’him’, governed by a preposition: ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ’from him’
αὐτός: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., masc. nom. sg.: ’he himself’
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὐτὴ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., fem. nom. sg.: ’she herself’, ’you yourself’
αὐτὴν: αὐτός — self; fem. acc. sg.: ’her’ · also intensive, accusative subject of an infinitive: ’she herself’ (αὐτὴν ποθέσαι ’that she herself miss [him]’)
αὐτῶν: αὐτός — self; gen. pl.: ’their own’ (reinforcing a possessive) · also plain neut. gen. pl. personal pronoun, not reinforcing a possessive: ’them’ (λήσομαι αὐτῶν ’I will forget them’, of things said)
αὖτε: αὖτε — again, in turn, on the other hand; adv.
βασιλῆα: βασιλεύς — king; acc. sg., epic βασιλῆα (= Attic βασιλέα)
βασιλῆας: βασιλεύς — king, chief; masc. acc. pl., epic -ῆας (= Attic -εῖς)
βασιλῆος: βασιλεύς — king; masc. gen. sg., epic -ῆος (= Attic -έως)
βαῖνε: βαίνω — go, walk, step; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔβαινε); here tmesis μετέβαινε ’was following’ · also without tmesis: ’went’ (ἀμφ’ ἑνὶ δούρατι βαῖνε ’went astride one timber’)
γέρας: γέρας — privilege, honor, due portion; neut. nom./acc. sg.
γαίης: γαῖα — earth, land; gen. sg. (Ionic η for α)
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γείνατο: γείνομαι — beget, bear (of a mother); aor. 3 sg. mid., epic, unaugmented (= ἐγείνατο)
γλαυκῶπις: γλαυκῶπις — epithet of Athena: ’gleaming-eyed’ (or ’owl-eyed’; sense uncertain); fem. nom. sg.
γρῆυς: γραῦς (epic γρῆυς) — old woman; nom. sg.
γυναικῶν: γυνή — woman; fem. gen. pl., partitive with δῖα: ’heavenly-one of women’
δένδρεα: δένδρεον — tree; neut. nom./acc. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic δένδρα)
δή: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δήεις: δήω (defective) — find; pres. with future sense, 2 sg., epic (= Attic εὑρήσεις): ’you will find’
δαινυμένους: δαίνυμι — give a feast; mid. δαίνυμαι, feast, banquet; pres. part. mid. masc. acc. pl.: ’feasting’
δείξω: δείκνυμι — show, point out; fut. 1 sg.: ’I will show’
δεινὴ: δεινός — dread, terrible, awesome; fem. nom. sg.
δεύεται: δεύω — wet, moisten; pres. 3 sg. mid. with retained acc. (πτερὰ δεύεται): ’wets its (own) wings’ · also pres. 3 sg. mid./pass.: ’is drenched’ (ὄμβρῳ δεύεται ’is drenched by rain’)
διαμπερές: διαμπερές — right through, clean through; adv.
διὰ: διά — through, throughout; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: διὰ … τινάξῃ = διατινάξῃ ’shake apart, shatter’
δμωαὶ: δμῳή — female servant, maid; fem. nom. pl. (cf. Attic δμωΐς)
δόρπον: δόρπον — evening meal, supper; neut. acc. sg.
δύω: δύο — two; numeral, epic by-form δύω, indeclinable
δώμαθ: δῶμα — house, home; neut. acc. pl., elided (δώμαθ’ = δώματα before a rough breathing)
δώματ: δῶμα — house, home; neut. acc. pl., elided (δώματ’ = δώματα) · also neut. nom. pl., subject: κλυτὰ δώματ’ ἔασιν ’his famous halls are’
δώματα: δῶμα — house, dwelling; neut. acc. pl. (plural for a single dwelling): ’house, home’
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῖος: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; masc. nom. sg., epithet of heroes (= fem. δῖα)
δῶκεν: δίδωμι — give; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔδωκεν)
δῶμα: δῶμα — house, hall, dwelling; acc. sg.
εἰ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. · also introducing an indirect question after a verb of asking or telling: ’whether’ (εἰ δή ’whether indeed’) · also in εἰ δ’ ἄγε, an interjectional idiom with the imperative: ’come now, well then’
εἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. (accented εἴ before a following enclitic, περ among them) · also introducing an indirect question, ‘whether’ (τίς δ’ οἶδ’ εἴ κέ ... ‘who knows whether’)
εἴη: εἰμί — be; pres. opt. 3 sg.: ’it might be, he might be’; impersonal + inf.: ’it might be possible for him’
εἶδος: εἶδος — form, look, beauty; neut. acc. sg. (accusative of respect): ’in beauty’
εὐρυάγυιαν: εὐρυάγυιος — wide-streeted (of a city); fem. acc. sg. εὐρυάγυιαν, agreeing with πόλιν (εὐρύς + ἄγυια ’street’)
θ: τε (elided and aspirated θ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — and; connective particle
θαύμαζεν: θαυμάζω — marvel, wonder; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic ἐθαύμαζε)
θαῦμα: θαῦμα — wonder, marvel; neut. nom. sg., in apposition: ’a wonder to see’
θεά: θεά — goddess; nom. sg. · also voc. sg. (same form): ’goddess!’
θεοῖο: θεός — god; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ) · also of a goddess, θεός being common in gender
θεοῦ: θεός — god; masc. gen. sg., genitive with a verb of hearing · also genitive governed by a preposition (ἄνευ θεοῦ ’without a god’) · also possessive genitive with a noun: ’of the god’ (θεοῦ δαῖτα)
θεσπεσίην: θεσπέσιος — wondrous, more than human (lit. god-uttered); fem. acc. sg.
θοὴν: θοός — swift, quick; fem. acc. sg.
θυμῷ: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; dat. sg.
θυράων: θύρα — door; fem. gen. pl., epic -άων (= Attic θυρῶν)
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κέν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic
κίε: κίω — go, go one’s way; aor. 3 sg. (root aorist, unaugmented): ’went’ (the gen. Τηλεμάχοιο is governed by ἰθύς ’straight toward’, not by this verb) · also imper. 2 sg.: ’go!’
καθ: κατά (elided καθ’) — down, throughout; prep. + acc., aspirated before rough breathing
καρπαλίμως: καρπάλιμος — swift, nimble; adv. καρπαλίμως: ’swiftly, nimbly’
κατέχευε: καταχέω — pour down over; aor. 3 sg., epic (= Attic κατέχεεν), augmented, + dat.: ’shed upon’
κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, in; prep. + acc.; also as preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἤσθιον = κατήσθιον ’devoured’) · also ’according to, in conformity with’ (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’) · also + acc., ’in quest of, after’ (κατὰ ληίδα ’in quest of plunder’)
κείνη: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); fem. nom. sg.
κελεύεις: κελεύω — bid, command, order; pres. 2 sg.
κιχήσεαι: κιχάνω — come upon, reach, find; fut. mid. 2 sg. (κιχήσεαι = Attic κιχήσῃ): ’you shall find, come upon’
κούρην: κούρη — girl, daughter (epic = Attic κόρη); fem. acc. sg.
κοῦροι: κοῦρος — young man, boy; nom. pl.
κρῆναι: κρήνη — spring, fountain; fem. nom. pl.
κῆπον: κῆπος — garden, orchard; masc. acc. sg.
κῆρ: κῆρ — heart; neut. acc. sg., accusative of respect (φίλον κῆρ ’in his own heart’) · also neut. nom. sg., subject of a verb: κῆρ ἤθελε ’my heart wished’
κῆρι: κῆρ — heart; neut. dat. sg., in the fixed adverbial idiom περὶ κῆρι ’exceedingly, at heart’ (περί used adverbially)
λαὸν: λαός — people, host; masc. acc. sg.
λαῖτμα: λαῖτμα — the gulf, the deep (of the sea); neut. nom./acc. sg.
λαῶν: λαός — people, host; masc. gen. pl., governed by ἄνασσε ’was lord over’ · also gen. with a noun: ’of the people’ (ποιμένα λαῶν ’shepherd of the people’)
λύει: λύω — loose, dissolve; pres. 3 sg. (of an assembly): ’dismisses’
μάλ: μάλα (elided μάλ’) — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μέγ: μέγας — great; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially, elided (μέγ’ = μέγα): ’greatly’ · also plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. noun, not adverbial: κῦμα μέγ’ ’a great wave’
μέγας: μέγας — great, big, grown; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’grown’ · also plain attributive adj., masc. nom. sg., ’great, huge’ (μέγας σῦς ’a great boar’), not predicate
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ (the acute μέν is kept before a following enclitic; elsewhere μὲν) · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’ (οὐ μέν ’not indeed’)
μένος: μένος — force, might, spirit, drive; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject (μένος … ἐνέστακται ’his force has been instilled’)
μή: μή — not; negative particle (used with imperatives and subjunctives, unlike οὐ) · also introducing a negative purpose/fear clause with the optative in secondary sequence: μή ἑ λάθοι ’lest he should escape notice’ · also μή + fut. inf. after a verb of swearing/promising, negating its content: μή ... βουλευσέμεν ’that ... will not plan’ · also ’lest’ with the subj. after a primary verb (μή πώς ... χαλεπήνῃ ’lest he be harsh’) · also in a question expecting the answer ’no’, after ἦ: ἦ μή … φάσθ’ ἔμμεναι; ’surely you do not say … are?’
μίαν: εἷς, μία, ἕν — one; numeral, fem. acc. sg.
μίν: μιν — him; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν), accented μίν, subject of the inf. ἀνάξασθαι in indirect statement
μακρὰ: μακρός — long, tall, high; neut. nom./acc. pl. (δούρατα μακρὰ ’long timbers’)
μεγάροισιν: μέγαρον — hall, great room, house; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν), plural for a single house
μεγάρῳ: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. dat. sg.
μεγαλήτορος: μεγαλήτωρ — great-hearted, great of spirit (μέγας + ἦτορ ’heart’); masc. gen. sg.
μετ: μετά (elided μετ’) — among, after, in quest of; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (μετ’ … βαῖνε = μετέβαινε ’followed’) · also + dat., ’among, between’ (μετ’ ἀμφοτέροισιν ’between the two of them’)
μετὰ: μετά — among, with, after; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · with acc. also ’in quest of, in search of’ (μετὰ χαλκόν ’after bronze’) · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’
μηδ: μηδέ — and not, nor; neg. conj., elided (μηδ’ = μηδέ)
μηδέ: μηδέ — and not, nor, do not; neg. conj., used to forbid before an imperative
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’
μύθοισιν: μῦθος — word, speech; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
μύθων: μῦθος — speech, word, thing said (not yet ’myth’ in Homer); gen. pl.
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
νέες: ναῦς — ship; fem. nom. pl., epic νέες (= Attic νῆες)
ναυσίθοος: Ναυσίθοος — Nausithous, founder of the Phaeacian city; nom. sg.
ναυσικάαν: Ναυσικάα — Nausicaa, daughter of Alcinous; acc. sg.
νηυσὶ: ναῦς — ship; dat. pl., epic νηυσί (= Attic ναυσί)
νόημα: νόημα — thought, notion, idea; neut. nom. sg.
νόου: νόος — mind (Attic contracted νοῦ); gen. sg., uncontracted
νύκτας: νύξ — night; fem. acc. pl., acc. of time: ’by nights’
νῆα: ναῦς — ship; acc. sg., epic νῆα
νῆας: ναῦς — ship; fem. acc. pl., epic νῆας (= Attic ναῦς)
ξείνους: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend (epic = Attic ξένος); masc. acc. pl.
ξεῖνε: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend (epic = Attic ξένος); voc. sg.
ξεῖνος: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend (epic = Attic ξένος); nom. sg.
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’) · also encl. dat. sg. fem. ’to/for her’ (ἥ οἱ ὁμηλικίη ’who was of an age with her’)
οἳ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl.
οἴην: οἶος — alone, only; fem. acc. sg.
οἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl. · also encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (= οἱ, accented οἵ in this position) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; masc. nom. pl. ’they’, demonstrative: οἵ γ’ ὑβρισταί ’are they violent?’
οἵδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., masc. nom. pl.: ’these here’
οἶδα: οἶδα — know; perf. with pres. sense, 1 sg.: ’I know’
οἶκον: οἶκος — house, household (and its stores); acc. sg.
οἷά: οἷος — of what kind, such as; relative/exclamatory adj., neut. nom./acc. pl., with τε in a comparison: ’just as, like’
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐδὲ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj. (grave, mid-clause form)
οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)
οὓς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. acc. pl.
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὕνεκα: οὕνεκα (crasis of οὗ ἕνεκα) — because; also relative: for the sake of which, for which reason; conj.
οὗ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. gen. sg.: ’whose’ (= Attic οὗ) · also neut. gen. sg. in ἐξ οὗ ’since, from the time when’
οὗτος: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; masc. nom. sg.
πάντα: πᾶς — all, every; neut. nom./acc. pl.
πέλεν: πέλω — be, become; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented: ’was’
πέρι: περί — around, about, exceedingly; adv. with anastrophe (accent thrown back): ’beyond all others’ (πέρι κέρδεα οἶδεν) · also preposition with anastrophe + acc., of place: ’around’ (ἄστυ πέρι ’around the city’)
παλλὰς: Παλλάς — Pallas, title of Athena of unknown origin (perhaps πάλλω ’brandish’); nom. sg.
παρὰ: παρά — beside, along, from; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · also used as an adverb with no case expressed: ’beside, alongside’ (παρὰ … ἐτάνυσσε τράπεζαν ’drew a table up beside (them)’)
πατρίδα: πατρίς — native land, fatherland; fem. acc. sg. (φίλην ... πατρίδα γαῖαν ’his dear fatherland’)
παῖδα: παῖς — child, son, daughter; masc./fem. acc. sg.
περ: περ — even, though; concessive particle, esp. with a participle (= Attic καίπερ) · also used to intensify an adverb or pronoun rather than concede a point: ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’
περικαλλέα: περικαλλής — very beautiful; fem. acc. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic περικαλλῆ) · also neut. nom./acc. pl., agreeing with a neuter plural noun: ’very beautiful’ (ἔργα ... περικαλλέα ’very beautiful works, fine handiwork’)
περὶ: περί — around, about; prep. + gen.: ’superior to, beyond’; also as adv.: ’exceedingly, surpassingly’ · also prep. + gen. in its plain sense ’about, concerning’ (περὶ πατρός ’about his father’) · also preverb in tmesis · + dat. · also + acc., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ ἄστυ ’around the city’) · also + gen., of place, physically ’around, encircling’ (περὶ σπείους γλαφυροῖο ’around the hollow cave’), distinct from the comparative ’beyond’ sense above · also + dat. in the fixed idiom περὶ κῆρι ’exceedingly, at heart’ (περὶ κῆρι τιμήσουσιν ’will honor him at heart’) · also + dat., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ χροῒ ’about the skin’)
ποθ: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; enclitic adv., elided before a rough breathing (ποθ’ = ποτέ)
ποθεν: πόθεν — from somewhere; indefinite enclitic adv. (accentless after εἰ), distinct from interrogative πόθεν ’from where?’
ποιήσατ: ποιέω — make; aor. 3 sg. mid., elided (ποιήσατ’ = ποιήσατο)
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.: ’many things, greatly’ · also neut. nom. pl., plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. pl. noun (πολλὰ ... δάκρυα ’many tears’)
πολλὴν: πολύς — much, many; fem. acc. sg.
πολύτλας: πολύτλας — much-enduring; adj., masc. nom. sg., standing epithet of Odysseus (πολύ ’much’ + root of τλῆναι ’endure’)
ποσειδάων: Ποσειδῶν — Poseidon, god of the sea, enemy of Odysseus after the blinding of his son Polyphemus; nom. sg., epic uncontracted
ποτ: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; enclitic adv., elided (ποτ’ = ποτέ)
ποτε: ποτέ — once, at some time, formerly; enclitic adv.
προθύροισι: πρόθυρον — forecourt, porch; neut. dat. pl.
προσέειπε: προσεῖπον — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic προσεῖπε)
προτὶ: πρός (epic by-form προτί) — towards, to; prep. + acc.
πρὶν: πρίν — before, until; adv./conj., + inf. (grave, mid-clause form) · also τὸ πρίν, substantivized with the article: ‘formerly, at first’, no infinitive · also bare adv. ’formerly’, no art./inf.
πρὸς: πρός — towards, against, to; prep. + acc. · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also + dat.: πρὸς ἀλλήλῃσιν ἔχονται ’cling close to one another’ · also + gen., ’from, under the protection of’ (πρὸς Διός εἰσιν ’are from Zeus’)
πρῶτα: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’first’
πυκινὸν: πυκινός — thick, close-set, solid; masc. acc. sg.: ’solid’
πόλινδ: πόλις — city; fem. acc. sg. with -δε suffix, elided (πόλινδ’ = πόλινδε): ’to the city’
πόντον: πόντος — sea, open sea; acc. sg.
πόντῳ: πόντος — sea, open sea; dat. sg.
πᾶσιν: πᾶς — all, every; masc./neut. dat. pl. (ν-movable)
σιγῇ: σιγή — silence; fem. dat. sg. used adverbially: ’in silence’
στῆ: ἵστημι — set, stand; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔστη): ’stood’
σφισι: σφεῖς — they; epic encl. dat. pl. pron. (= Attic αὐτοῖς): ’to/for them’
σχερίην: Σχερίη — Scheria, the Phaeacians’ island; fem. acc. sg.
σὴν: σός — your, yours; fem. acc. sg.
σὺ: σύ — you (sg.); nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’)
τάων: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); fem. gen. pl., epic (= Attic τῶν): ’of these/those women’
τέκος: τέκος — child, offspring; neut. voc. sg. (φίλον τέκος ’dear child’)
τήν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg., resumptive: ’whom’ · also demonstrative, fem. acc. sg., resuming an earlier noun: ’her’ (τήν … ῥέξω ’her I will sacrifice’)
τήνδε: ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε — this (here); demonstrative pron., fem. acc. sg.
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τηλόθεν: τηλόθεν — from afar, from a distance; adv., ablatival suffix -θεν
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’ · also adjectival indefinite: ’some, any’ (τι δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’) · also adverbial without a negative: ’in some way, in some measure’ (τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ’on some business’) · also as a substantive object, in a question: ’anything, something’ (ἦ ῥά τι ἴδμεν ’do we know anything’) · also the neut. of τις forming, with a preceding ὅ, the indefinite relative ὅ τι ’whatever, that which’ (αὔδα ὅ τι φρονέεις ’say whatever you have in mind’)
τιν: τις, τι — someone, something; neut./masc. acc. sg., elided (τιν’ = τινα)
τινα: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., indefinite: ’whatever one’ · also masc./fem. acc. sg. ’someone, some’; after a relative, ὅν τινα, ἥν τινα (= ὅντινα, ἥντινα), part of ὅστις: ’what, whatever’
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg.
τοί: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. pl. ’they’ · also relative: ’who’ · also encl. dat. sg. pron. σύ ’to you’ (= τοι, accented before a following enclitic, e.g. τοί τι)
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοιγὰρ: τοιγάρ — well then, accordingly; particle introducing a response to a request
τοκήων: τοκεύς — parent, begetter; masc. gen. pl.
τοῖον: τοῖος — such, of such a kind; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’in such a way’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a noun or pronoun: ’such a one as’ (σέ γε τοῖον ἐγείνατο ’bore a son such as you’) · also ’so’, qualifying an adj. · also neut. nom./acc. sg., agreeing with a neut. noun: τοῖον … ἔρνος (acc.), τοῖον … δόρυ (nom.) ’such a shoot, such a trunk’
τοῖσδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., masc./neut. dat. pl.: ’these’
τοῖσι: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’to/among them’
τοῖχον: τοῖχος — wall (of a room or house); acc. sg.
τότ: τότε — then, at that time; adv., elided (τότ’ = τότε)
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’)
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’ · also ’it’, of a thing (τὴν = the clothing): fem. acc. sg. · also with a noun, article-like: τὴν ὁδόν ’that journey’
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’) · also demonstrative adjective with a noun: ’that, the’ (τὸν μῦθον ’that story, message’)
τῆς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); fem. gen. sg.
τῇ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. dat. sg.: ’her, with her’ · also adverbial, ’there, in that place’, pointing back to a place just named (τῇ τόν γε μένον λοχόωντες ’there they lay in wait for him’) · also relative, fem. dat. sg., serving as an instrumental, ’with which’ (ῥάβδον, τῇ τ’ ἀνδρῶν ὄμματα θέλγει ’a wand, with which he charms men’s eyes’), not the personal pronoun
τῶν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); gen. pl. ’of these things, of them’ · also with a noun, article-like: τῶν ἄλλων ἀνέμων ’of the other winds’
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’)
φέρεν: φέρω — bring, carry; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔφερε): ’was bringing’
φίλα: φίλος — dear, one’s own; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially with φρονέω: ’with friendly thoughts, kindly’ · also plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. pl. noun: ’dear’ (τέκνα φίλα ’dear children’)
φίλους: φίλος — dear, one’s own; substantival masc. acc. pl.: ’dear ones, kin’
φίλων: φίλος — dear, one’s own; masc. gen. pl. (φίλοι ’kin, dear ones’)
φαίηκες: Φαίηξ — a Phaeacian; masc. nom. pl.
φαιήκων: Φαίηξ — a Phaeacian; masc. gen. pl.
φρένας: φρήν — mind, heart, wits (lit. midriff); fem. acc. pl.
φρονέουσ: φρονέω — think, be minded, ponder; pres. part. fem. nom. sg., elided, uncontracted (φρονέουσ’ = φρονέουσα)
φρονέῃσ: φρονέω — think, be minded; pres. subj. 3 sg., epic -ῃσι (= Attic -ῇ), elided (φρονέῃσ’ = φρονέῃσι)
φωνήσασ: φωνέω — utter, speak aloud, raise one’s voice; aor. part. fem. nom. sg., elided (φωνήσασ’ = φωνήσασα)
χάλκεον: χάλκεος — of bronze; masc./neut. acc. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic χαλκοῦν)
χεῦε: χέω — pour; aor. 3 sg., here in tmesis (ἐπὶ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε): ‘poured upon’
χθονὶ: χθών — earth, ground; fem. dat. sg.
χώρῳ: χῶρος — place, spot; masc. dat. sg.
ἀγήρως: ἀγήραος — ageless, not growing old (ἀ- + γῆρας); masc./fem. nom. sg., contracted ἀγήρως
ἀγακλυτὰ: ἀγακλυτός — very renowned, glorious; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἀγλαὰ: ἀγλαός — splendid, shining, glorious; adj., neut. acc. pl. (ἀγλαὰ δῶρα ’splendid gifts’)
ἀγορὰς: ἀγορή — assembly; fem. acc. pl. (Attic ἀγοράς)
ἀθήνη: Ἀθήνη — Athena, goddess of wisdom and war; nom. sg.
ἀθήνην: Ἀθήνη — Athena, goddess of wisdom and war; acc. sg.
ἀθανάτοις: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; adj., masc. dat. pl.
ἀθανάτους: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc. acc. pl., substantival: ’the immortals’
ἀλκίνοος: Ἀλκίνοος — Alcinous, king of the Phaeacians; nom. sg.
ἀλκινόοιο: Ἀλκίνοος — Alcinous, king of the Phaeacians; gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἀλκινόου: Ἀλκίνοος — Alcinous, king of the Phaeacians; masc. gen. sg.
ἀμείνων: ἀγαθός — good; comparative ἀμείνων, masc. nom. sg.: ’better’
ἀμφιέλισσαι: ἀμφιέλισσα — curved on both sides (or rowed both ways); sense uncertain; fem. nom. pl., epithet of ships
ἀμφοτέρωθεν: ἀμφότερος — both; adv. with suffix -θεν: ’on both sides’
ἀμφὶ: ἀμφί — on both sides, around, about; prep./adv. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἀμφὶ ... βάλλομεν = ἀμφιβάλλομεν ’we threw around, embraced’)
ἀμφὶς: ἀμφίς — apart, on both sides, around; adverb
ἀμύμονος: ἀμύμων — blameless, excellent (an old epithet whose exact force is uncertain); gen. sg.
ἀνάσσει: ἀνάσσω — be lord, rule (+ dat.); pres. 3 sg.
ἀνέρος: ἀνήρ — man; masc. gen. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἀνδρός)
ἀνδράσι: ἀνήρ — man; masc. dat. pl., epic ἀνδράσι
ἀνθρώποισι: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ἀνθρώπους: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; acc. pl.
ἀνθρώπων: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; gen. pl.
ἀντιβολήσας: ἀντιβολέω — meet, encounter; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’who meets (us)’
ἀνὰ: ἀνά — up along, throughout; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis (ἀνὰ … κέρασσεν, from ἀνακεράννυμι ’mix up’)
ἀπέβη: ἀποβαίνω — go away, depart; aor. 3 sg., augment inside the compound (ἀπ-έ-βη)
ἀπήνης: ἀπήνη — mule-wagon, cart; fem. gen. sg.
ἀρίστη: ἄριστος — best; superl., fem. nom. sg.
ἀργύρεον: ἀργύρεος — silver, made of silver; adj., masc. acc. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἀργυροῦν)
ἀτάσθαλον: ἀτάσθαλος — wanton, reckless, presumptuous; masc. acc. sg., adjectival (distinct from the noun ἀτασθαλίαι)
ἀτρύγετον: ἀτρύγετος — unharvested (epithet of the sea; sense disputed); masc. acc. sg., agreeing with πόντον
ἄλλα: ἄλλος — other, another; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἄλλας: ἄλλος — other, another; fem. acc. pl.
ἄλλη: ἄλλος — other, another; fem. nom. sg., adverbial in the idiom ἄλλυδις ἄλλη ’one this way, another that’
ἄλλοθεν: ἄλλοθεν — from elsewhere, from another place; adv. (ἄλλος + -θεν ’from’)
ἄν: ἄν — modal particle marking contingency (with subj. = future contingency, with opt. = potential)
ἄνασσε: ἀνάσσω — be lord over, rule; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented, + gen.: ’was lord over’
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, elided form ἄρ’ before a vowel · also the shortened form ἄρ used, without true elision, before τε in the fixed collocation ἄρ τε: τὰ μὲν ἄρ τε διεσκέδασ’
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄστυ: ἄστυ — town, city; neut. acc. sg.
ἅπαντα: ἅπας — all, the whole of; masc. acc. sg. · also neut. nom./acc. pl., subject or object of a verb: ’all things’ (τελευτηθῆναι ἅπαντα ’that all things were fulfilled’)
ἐίσας: ἐΐσος — well-balanced, even (sense disputed, perhaps ’equal on both sides’); fem. acc. pl. ἐίσας, agreeing with νῆας
ἐγείνατο: γείνομαι — beget, bear; aor. 3 sg. mid., augmented: ’bore’
ἐγώ: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg. (accented ἐγώ before the enclitic τοι that follows)
ἐικυῖα: ἔοικα — be like, resemble; perf. part. fem. nom. sg., + dat.: ’likened to, having the appearance of’
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐλπωρή: ἐλπωρή — hope, expectation; fem. nom. sg.
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνθάδ: ἐνθάδε (elided ἐνθάδ’) — here, to this place; adv.
ἐνοσίχθων: ἐνοσίχθων — earth-shaker, epithet of Poseidon (from ἔνοσις ’shaking’ + χθών ’earth’); nom. sg.
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat.
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐπ’ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε ‘poured upon’)
ἐπέεσσι: ἔπος — word, speech; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic ἔπεσι)
ἐπίστασθαι: ἐπίσταμαι — know, understand, be skilled in; pres. inf.
ἐπηετανὸν: ἐπηετανός — continuous, unfailing, year-long; neut. acc. sg.
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’)
ἐρέεινε: ἐρεείνω — question, ask; impf. 3 sg. act., unaugmented: ’questioned, was questioning’
ἐρατεινήν: ἐρατεινός — lovely, charming; fem. acc. sg.
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐσθῆτά: ἐσθής — clothing, raiment; fem. acc. sg.
ἐυπλόκαμος: ἐϋπλόκαμος — fair-tressed, with fine hair; fem. nom. sg. (Calypso’s standing epithet) · also used of Demeter (5.125), so not unique to Calypso despite the parenthetical above
ἐφ: ἐπί (elided ἐφ’ before a rough breathing) — on, upon, over; + acc. · also + dat., with anastrophe (χερσὶ ἐφ’ ὕδωρ): ’over, upon (the hands)’
ἐόντα: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc./neut. acc. sg., epic (= Attic ὄντα)
ἐὺ: ἐΰ — well (Attic εὖ, printed without a diaeresis); adv.
ἑὸν: ἑός — his own, her own (possessive, by-form of ὅς); masc. acc. sg. · also neut. acc./nom. sg., agreeing with a neuter noun (δῶμα ἑὸν ’his own hall’)
ἔδοντες: ἔδω — eat (epic, = Attic ἐσθίω); pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’eating’
ἔκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; prep. + gen., placed after its pronoun with anastrophe: τοῦ ... ἔκ = ἐκ τοῦ ’from him’ · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἔκ … ὀνόμαζε = ἐξωνόμαζε ’called by name’)
ἔλαιον: ἔλαιον — olive oil; neut. acc. sg.
ἔλθοι: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. opt. 3 sg. (wish): ’may... come’
ἔμελλε: μέλλω — be about to, be destined to (+ inf.); impf. 3 sg.: ’was destined, was about to’
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also used relatively, continuing a clause: ’where’ (ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’)
ἔπι: ἐπί — on, upon, over; prep. + dat., placed after its noun with anastrophe: ἑοῖς ἔπι ’upon his own (possessions)’ · also + gen., postpositive with anastrophe, of direction: ’toward’ (νήσου ἔπι Ψυρίης ’toward the island of Psyria’) · also as adverb with no case expressed, intensifying repetition: ’besides, again’ (ἔπι δεύτερον αὖτις ’a second time, once more’)
ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἔσαν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἦσαν)
ἔστιν: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg., impersonal: ’it is possible’ · also plain copula, personal: ’is’ (ἀργύρεος ... ἔστιν ἅπας ’it is entirely silver’)
ἔχοντες: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.
ἕρκος: ἕρκος — fence, barrier, enclosure; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἕστασαν: ἵστημι — stand; pluperf. 3 pl., intransitive, with simple past force: ’were standing’ (reduplicated ἑ-στα-σαν)
ἕτερον: ἕτερος — the other (of two); masc./neut. acc. sg.
ἠελίου: ἥλιος (epic ἠέλιος) — sun; masc. gen. sg.
ἠλάκατα: ἠλάκατα — spun wool, yarn (neut. pl.; cf. ἠλακάτη ’distaff’); neut. acc. pl.
ἠρᾶτο: ἀράομαι — pray, vow; impf. 3 sg., augmented (ἀ- → ἠ-)
ἠὲ: ἠέ — or; epic conj. (= Attic ἤ)
ἡ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. sg.: ’she’
ἡγήσατο: ἡγέομαι — lead the way, go before; aor. 3 sg.
ἡγεμονεύσω: ἡγεμονεύω — lead the way, guide; fut. 1 sg.: ’I will lead’
ἡμιόνοιιν: ἡμίονος — mule; dual gen./dat., epic -οιιν (= Attic -οιν): ’of the two mules’
ἣ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
ἤγαγον: ἄγω — lead, bring; aor. 3 pl., reduplicated
ἤματα: ἦμαρ — day; neut. acc. pl., acc. of time: ’all the days, every day’
ἥ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. · also ὁ, ἡ, τό (personal/demonstrative pronoun): she; fem. nom. sg. (ἥ γε ’she indeed’, of the ship)
ἥφαιστος: Ἥφαιστος — Hephaestus, god of the forge; nom. sg.
ἦρχε: ἄρχω — begin, rule; impf. 3 sg., + gen. ’began (the speaking)’ · also ’go first, lead the way’ (no gen.): ἦρχε δ’ Ἀθήνη ’and Athena went first, led the way’ · also + gen. of the way: ἦρχε ὁδοῖο ’led the way’ · also absolute: ’ruled, was king’
ἰδέειν: ὁράω (aor. stem εἰδ-) — see; aor. inf., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἰδεῖν)
ἰδέσθαι: ὁράω — see; aor. mid. inf.: ‘to see’
ἱκάνω: ἱκάνω (poetic by-form of ἱκνέομαι) — come to, arrive at, reach; pres. 1 sg.
ἱκέσθαι: ἱκνέομαι — come to, reach, arrive at; aor. inf.
ἴμεν: εἶμι — go; pres. inf., epic (= Attic ἰέναι)
ἴχνια: ἴχνιον — footprint, track; neut. acc. pl.
ἵκανε: ἱκάνω — come to, reach; impf. 3 sg.: ’came upon’
ἵκετο: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive at, reach; aor. 3 sg.; where the metre makes the ι long, that is the augment, which the spelling cannot show; with short ι, unaugmented
ἵκοντο: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive at, reach; aor. 3 pl.; with short ι (by metre) unaugmented; where the metre makes the ι long, augmented (the spelling cannot show it)
ὀδυσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. nom. sg., single-σ metrical variant Ὀδυσεύς
ὀδυσσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσῆι: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; dat. sg. (single-σ metrical variant of Ὀδυσσῆι)
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg.
ὁδὸν: ὁδός — way, journey; fem. acc. sg.
ὁπλοτάτη: ὁπλότερος (superl. ὁπλότατος) — younger, youngest; fem. nom. sg.
ὃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also plain demonstrative, ’he’ (ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν), not a relative
ὄνομ: ὄνομα — name; neut. nom. sg., elided (ὄνομ’ = ὄνομα), subject of λίπηται: ’his name’
ὅθεν: ὅθεν — from where, whence; relative adv.
ὅν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron. (indefinite with τε/τις: ὅν τινα = ὅστις, ’whatever’); masc. acc. sg., accented before enclitic τινά · also plain relative pron., masc. acc. sg., not accented for a following enclitic: ’whom’ (ὅν ῥα καθεῖσεν ’whom he had stationed’)
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.)
ὅσσαι: ὅσος (epic ὅσσος) — as much as, as many as; fem. nom. pl., epic geminated form ὅσσαι (= ὅσαι)
ὅσσον: ὅσος (epic ὅσσος) — as much/great as; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially, correlative with τόσσον: ’as far as’
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’) · also with the optative, hypothetical/conditional: ’if ever, whenever’ (ὅτε ... ἵκοι ’if ever such need should come upon me’)
ὅτις: ὅστις — whoever, whatever; masc. nom. sg., epic (ὅτις = Attic ὅστις)
ὑγρὸν: ὑγρός — wet, moist, flowing; adj., neut. nom./acc. sg. (agreeing with ὕδωρ) · also agreeing with ἔλαιον: ’liquid (oil)’
ὑπ: ὑπό (elided ὑπ’) — under, beneath; prep. + gen.; also + acc., ’under, up under’ · also of agent with a verb of dying, ‘by, at the hands of’ + gen. (ὤλεθ’ ὑπ’ Αἰγίσθοιο ‘perished by Aegisthus’) · also + dat., ’under, beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb, no case governed: οὓς ὑπ’ Ὀδυσσεὺς δύσετ’ = ὑπεδύσετο ’underneath which Odysseus sank down’
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’) · also plain ὡς + indic., ’as’ (ὡς σὺ κελεύεις ’as you command’) or ’how’ in an indirect question (ὡς ἐπὶ πόντον ἐλεύσομαι ’how I shall come upon the sea’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν μὴ κλαίουσα κατὰ χρόα καλὸν ἰάπτῃς ’so that you might not mar your fair skin with weeping’) · also ὡς δ’ ὅτε introducing an epic simile, ’as when’, its clause taking indic. or ἄν/κε + subj. for a general case: ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ ἂν ... φανήῃ ’as when ... should appear’ · also comparative ’like’, placed after the noun it compares (ἀνέμου ὡς πνοιή ’like a blast of wind’)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ὤλετο: ὄλλυμι — destroy; mid. perish, be lost; aor. 3 sg. mid., augmented: ’has perished, is gone’
ὥς: ὥς — thus, so; also (with κε/ἄν + subj.) ’so that, in order that’; adverb/conjunction · also introducing an indirect question: ’how’ (ὥς κε νέηται ’how he is to return’, after φράσσεται) · or ὡς ’as’, accented before enclitic τε · also causal, ’since, seeing that’ (ὥς οἱ ἐναργὲς ὄνειρον ἐπέσσυτο ’since a vivid dream had come upon her’)
ὦρτο: ὄρνυμι — stir up, rouse; mid./intr. aor. 3 sg. ὦρτο, root aorist: ’arose’ (of a wind springing up)
ᾗσι: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. dat. pl.: ’in his own (mind)’ (φρεσὶν ᾗσι)
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥά: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, weak enclitic form ῥα, accented ῥά
ῥα: ἄρα — then, so; weak enclitic form ῥα (used after a vowel)
